- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after sharp declines or spikes.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic (high) in the first 5–10 days, then drop sharply — suggesting overreaction to recent volatility.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing the true mean reversion trend, especially when prices are near historical lows.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward spikes in history — model predicts a peak too early and then overcorrects downward.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent low prices, leading to exaggerated downward bias when prices are already falling.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., consistent underperformance in late Q1 or early Q2.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model often underestimates the continuation or overestimates the correction.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture short-term volatility spikes or sudden reversals in the last 5–7 days.
- Model tends to overcorrect after a sharp drop, predicting a recovery too quickly or too aggressively.
- Forecasts are often too high in the middle of the 30-day window, especially when history shows a plateau or slow decline.
